Five adjoining freehold shophouses on Owen Road hit market at $33 mil
article:
A row of five freehold shophouses in Farrer Park is being offered for sale through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise.

Located at 96 Owen Road, the adjoining two-storey shophouses with four-storey rear extensions have a guide price of $33 million, or $1,962 psf on their existing total gross floor area of approximately 16,823 sq ft.

The shophouses occupy a 6,021 sq ft site zoned “Residential with commercial at first storey”. It has a plot ratio of 3.0.

The shophouses are fully occupied, said Cushman & Wakefield and CBRE, which are jointly marketing the properties. They feature five commercial units on the ground floor, while the upper floors, which are approved for Serviced Apartment II (SA2) use, offer accommodation managed by The Assembly Place.

“96 Owen Road presents a rare opportunity to acquire a freehold accommodation asset comprising five adjoining shophouses within the city fringe,” said Sophia Lim, Cushman & Wakefield Singapore’s director of capital markets. "The property's SA2 approval, coupled with its scale relative to typical shophouse investments, provides investors with immediate exposure to Singapore's growing living sector."

Joshua Giam, director of capital markets at CBRE Singapore, said that the ground-floor units could be repositioned for F&B use, subject to approvals from the relevant authorities.

The shophouses are 150m from Farrer Park MRT Station on the North-East Line. They are also near retail offerings at City Square Mall and Mustafa Centre , and healthcare facilities at Farrer Park Hospital and Connexion .

Giam noted that the shophouses are close to the Dorset Road Government Land Sale site that will introduce new homes and further rejuvenate the neighbourhood.

The site was awarded last October to a consortium comprising UOL Group, Singapore Land Group and Kheng Leong Co. The partners are expected to launch the 428-unit Dorset Gardens condo in the first half of 2027.

“The introduction of new private housing is likely to enhance the area's residential profile, attract a broader demographic of residents and support the continued uplift in property values and commercial activity,” said Giam.

The EOI will close at 3pm on Oct 27.

title: Freehold industrial building at Kampong Ampat launched for collective sale at $105 mil
article:
A freehold industrial building at 153 Kampong Ampat in the Tai Seng-MacPherson area has been launched for collective sale by public tender. The seven-storey multi-use industrial development has a guide price of $105 million.

The building sits on 43,354 sq ft of land zoned for Business 1 use with a plot ratio of 2.5. The property has an existing gross floor area of around 114,969 sq ft, translating to an existing plot ratio of approximately 2.65.

The guide price works out to a land rate of about $913 psf per plot ratio, said Knight Frank Singapore, the property’s marketing agent, in a Sept 28 release.

It added that authorities have indicated support for workers’ dormitory use at the site. This would be subject to approval of a detailed proposal and compliance with all applicable planning and regulatory requirements.

Occupying a corner plot bounded by Kampong Ampat and Upper Aljunied Link, the building has extensive road frontage and prominent visibility.

The strong performance of recent industrial launches and transactions reflects sustained demand for well-located freehold assets, particularly within established city-fringe precincts, noted Melvin Chay, senior director of capital markets at Knight Frank Singapore.

In July, freehold strata industrial project Generations @ Tannery saw all 54 production units and five canteen units taken up on its public launch day . Prices ranged from around $1,500 psf to $2,000 psf.

Other recent notable deals include the en bloc sale of Tan Boon Liat Building , a freehold industrial property at Outram Road, to Kingsford Group for $950 million in July.

In June, a freehold industrial building that formerly housed Fujifilm Asia Pacific’s headquarters was sold . The eight-storey building on New Industrial Road fetched $71 million, caveats showed.

Before that, Hwa Yew Industrial Building , a freehold, strata-titled six-storey building at 17 Mandai Estate , was sold for $72 million in May.

“With its scale, visibility and flexibility for owner occupation, redevelopment or potential workers’ dormitory use, 153 Kampong Ampat should attract interest from a diverse pool of purchasers,” said Chay.

The tender will close at 10am on Oct 23.

title: Centurion buys Hong Kong mixed-use development Yan Woo Building for HK$364 mil
article:
Centurion Corporation is buying Yan Woo Building, a commercial and residential development in North Point, Hong Kong, for HK$364 million ($59.4 million). The Singapore Exchange -listed company is purchasing the building through a 50:50 joint venture with Centurion Properties, its controlling shareholder.

In a bourse filing, Centurion says it plans to carry out progressive addition and alteration works to Yan Woo Building’s 42 apartment units, which will be turned into rental accommodation.

Completed in 2000, Yan Woo Building sits at the junction of Java Road and Tong Shui Road in North Point, a residential and commercial district on Hong Kong Island East. It occupies a land area of 3,426 sq ft that is held under a government lease of 75 years from Sept 5, 1921, renewable for a further 75 years.

The 26-storey building comprises 42 apartment units spanning a gross floor area (GFA) of approximately 26,070 sq ft and nine commercial units totalling 8,216 sq ft.

The commercial units occupy the ground to second floors and are leased out to a mix of food and beverage, pharmacy, telecommunications, veterinary services and convenience store operators.

Rents from the commercial units will provide a base of recurring income while Centurion carries out the enhancement works to the residential floors, added Kong Chee Min, the company’s CEO.

Yan Woo Building is a three-minute walk from the North Point Mass Transit Railway station. It is also a short walk from the North Point Promenade on the Victoria Harbour waterfront.

title: CDL to invest $5 bil, divest $6 bil of assets, optimise hospitality portfolio over three years
article:
Real estate giant City Developments Ltd (CDL) on Sept 28 announced an extensive three-year roadmap for 2027 to 2029, following its strategic review.

Named "Get+", the refreshed strategy focuses on key geographies — with Singapore at the core — and four sectors: residential, commercial, hospitality and living.

It will comprise $5 billion of investments and $6 billion of divestments, in addition to more than $6 billion of projected property development cash inflows from existing projects.

Fund management will also become a more significant part of CDL's capital model, comprising new and existing listed Reit platforms and an expanded private capital platform via funds, partnerships and joint ventures.

In this respect, CDL is targeting $10 billion in total assets under management (AUM) by 2029, essentially doubling from about $5 billion in AUM as of June 30, 2026. To achieve this, CDL will set up a dedicated fund management entity, with an investment committee and leadership team that will be directly responsible for AUM growth and financial accountability.

Investing into Singapore, China, Japan

Under the Get+ three-year roadmap, CDL is looking to deploy $5 billion of growth capital across the four sectors of residential, commercial, hospitality and living.

Its target allocation for this capital is 60% to Singapore, 30% to China and Japan, and 10% to other markets.

The group said these are markets where it has "established capabilities, local knowledge and opportunities to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns", with Singapore to remain the main market for new investments.

Rationalising portfolio to unlock value

At the same time, CDL is targeting $6 billion of divestments to "crystallise embedded value" and recycle capital from mature, non-core or underperforming assets.

Potential pathways include outright divestments, as well as seeding suitable assets into managed vehicles, where appropriate.

The target divestment mix comprises 45% in commercial assets, 30% in hospitality, 20% in legacy residential and others, and 5% in the living sector.

The group said it will take a disciplined, returns-driven approach, by retaining strategic assets that support recurring income and long-term value, enhancing assets with identifiable upside, and recycling capital where value is best realised.

On top of the divestment proceeds, CDL expects more than $6 billion of projected cash inflows through to 2029 from property development sales. This will be supported by future cash collections from contracted sales and its existing development pipeline — including five unlaunched projects in Singapore and two projects in China.

The property development sales, which are in addition to the more than $6 billion divestment target, will come from Singapore projects such as Newport Residences , Zyon Grand , Union Square Residences , The Orie , Lucerne Grand , Solano Grand executive condo (EC), Wynwood Grand EC, and the government land sale (GLS) sites at Tanjong Rhu Road and Peck Hay Road .

In China, they include projects at Xintiandi, Shanghai, with about 145 units and villas; as well as Hong Leong Larimar Centre with 648 units.

Optimising the hospitality portfolio

Hospitality is set to be a key area of focus under the Get+ strategy.

The group’s global hospitality portfolio spans 165 hotels with around 48,000 rooms, including 88 owned hotels. Of these, 54 hotels, including two opening in the next 12 months, are directly held by CDL and valued at about $8.6 billion (excluding hotels under CDL Hospitality Trusts and Millennium and Copthorne Hotels New Zealand).

CDL said it will adopt a "tailored approach" for each of its owned hotels, by retaining core assets, enhancing assets that have further potential, and divesting selected properties.

About $1.8 billion of hotel divestments are targeted through 2029, representing 30% of the group’s overall $6 billion divestment target.

In all, CDL is aiming to realise more than $1 billion of Patmi from divestment gains across the three-year roadmap.

title: YANGZIJIANG FINANCIAL: Share Buybacks Begin — What Is Management Signalling?
article:
Yangzijiang Financial has finally begun doing something that shareholders have been asking about for some time: buying back its own deeply discounted shares.

The latest purchase, on 25 Sept, was another

The maths makes buybacks compelling.

In other words, management's priority was to build the business first.

title: Sony to skip CES show after Honda EV venture dropped
article:
(Sept 28): Sony Group Corp is skipping the CES technology show in 2027, ending a decades-long presence at the Las Vegas electronics showcase in favour of a growing focus on entertainment content.

Neither Sony, whose products were first displayed at the inaugural conference in 1967, nor its affiliates plan to exhibit at CES in January, a spokesperson said, confirming an earlier report by the Nikkei. The PlayStation creator did not have its own booth at the show earlier this year but its joint venture with Honda Motor Co displayed the Afeela electric vehicle, a joint venture that has since been scrapped.

The decision to skip CES entirely will reconfigure the show floor at the world’s highest-profile gathering for consumer electronics. Sony has long occupied one of the largest booths at CES, and even as Japanese peers reduced their footprint, it remained a mainstay and attracted large crowds with its keynote events.

Sony also synced up with the broader trend across CES toward the automotive sector, using the show to promote its collaboration with Honda to jointly develop EVs. That project — one of Sony’s most prominent attempts to explore a new platform for content and AI-powered services — unravelled this year and the two companies said they would reassess the future of their joint venture, established in 2022.

“We continuously and strategically evaluate our approach to events and communications based on the needs and priorities of our diverse business,” Sony said in a statement. The company’s focus continues to evolve toward entertainment, intellectual property and technology geared to support creators, it said.

Sony’s business has shifted increasingly toward games, music and film, reducing the importance of CES as a venue to display its strategy. The company remains a key supplier of image sensors used in automobiles and executives have argued that vehicles could eventually help create new forms of entertainment inside cars.

See also: SK Hynix shares fall as subsidiary Solidigm’s potential US IPO sours mood

title: Temasek buys minority stake in Italian PE firm FSI
article:
(Sept 28): Singaporean state-owned investor Temasek Holdings has acquired a 9% stake in the management company of Italian private equity firm FSI for an undisclosed amount, according to a joint statement. It will also invest in the firm’s future funds.

Temasek is also an investor in FSI’s Scale-up Capital Solutions fund, which targets the smaller end of mid-market investments. FSI’s two existing flagship funds raised about €1.4 billion (US$1.6 billion or $2.04 billion) and €1.6 billion, respectively, FSI’s website showed.

Nagi Hamiyeh, president of Temasek Global Investments, said the firm had been backers of FSI’s funds since 2018. The Milan-based investor specialises in backing Italian mid-market businesses, which it defines as those with revenues of €70 million to €200 million, and earnings before interest, taxation, depreciation and amortization of €10 million to €30 million.

“We can leverage the Temasek platform, drawing on our sector capabilities and global networks to help Italian companies expand into new markets,” Hamiyeh said in the statement.

title: NSE shares slip below IPO price after lacklustre India debut
article:
(Sept 28): Shares of National Stock Exchange of India Ltd slipped below their initial public offering price on the third day of trading, extending a lacklustre start amid a broader equity selloff.

The stock fell as much as 1.8% to 1,761 rupees on Monday, below the IPO price of 1,785 rupees. Shareholders of the world’s busiest derivatives exchange sold 225.6 billion rupees of stock in the offering, which saw shares eke out a gain of 1.9% on their first day of trading last week.

The IPO, India’s second-biggest after Hyundai Motor India Ltd’s 278.6 billion-rupee offering in 2024, drew a relatively subdued response, particularly from retail investors. The main book attracted bids worth less than one trillion rupees, with state-run Life Insurance Corp of India emerging as the biggest bidder.

NSE’s move to go public coincided with a selloff in Indian equities that has pushed the benchmark Nifty 50 Index to a seven-month low. While the listing gave investors access to a key part of India’s fast-growing capital market, valuation concerns forced the company to scale back both the size of the offering and its price.

Analysts have also flagged near-term pressure on NSE’s cash equities, derivatives and margin-trading volumes, with the recently introduced Closing Auction Session weighing on broader trading activity. Still, the bourse commands a premium to global peers. NSE trades at about 30 times estimated fiscal 2029 earnings, roughly 65% above the 18 times for international exchanges, Macquarie said in a note last week.

See also: NSE shares rise in stock market debut after US$2.4 bil IPO

NSE officials have remained upbeat about the exchange’s prospects, saying a wave of regulatory tightening in India’s derivatives market is largely over. The bourse is regaining market share in equity options as traders adapt to the stricter rules, and the bourse is seeing a pickup in commodities, Chief Executive Officer Ashishkumar Chauhan said.

The slump in share price comes after NSE chairman Srinivas Injeti told reporters Friday that “IPO pricing was calibrated to balance the interests of investors and selling shareholders”.

title: EU stands ready to support bloc’s farm sector, Ireland says
article:
(Sept 28): Further European Union emergency support for the bloc’s agriculture sector depends on how market conditions develop, after extreme heat over the summer, according to the Ireland’s Agriculture Minister Martin Heydon.

“It does depend on a number of factors,” Heydon said in an interview with Bloomberg Television, when asked whether the EU would need to go further than measures already announced. “Europe I think stands ready to support our agriculture sector.”

Heydon highlighted the measures taken by the bloc, including relaxing EU state aid rules to allow countries to support their agriculture sectors. There has also been emergency aid to address high fertiliser prices following the Iran war and longer-term measures in a Fertilizer Action Plan.

Individual countries have taken their own support measures. Earlier this month, France allocated more than €1 billion (US$1.14 billion) to support farmers as a result of crop losses due to the extreme heat.

Europe’s agriculture sector has been battered by drought and heat waves this summer, hitting production at a time of higher input costs and elevated global grain prices due to escalating attacks between Russia and Ukraine in the Black Sea. Strikes on ships and infrastructure have curtailed exports from a region that accounts for a quarter of the world’s wheat shipments.

Ukraine’s Agriculture Minister Taras Vysotskyi will join EU agriculture ministers at a meeting in Brussels on Monday, where he’s expected to update his counterparts on the situation for the country’s grain exports.

See also: Bayer earnings beat estimates on crop science strength

Ireland holds the EU’s rotating presidency until the end of the year, making Heydon a key voice among ministers from the 27 EU member states.

title: SK Hynix shares fall as subsidiary Solidigm’s potential US IPO sours mood
article:
(Sept 28): SK Hynix Inc shares fell on Monday as media reports of a potential listing of the chipmaker’s US subsidiary added to concerns over its complex ownership structure.

SK Hynix shares dropped 5%, the most in two weeks, after Bloomberg confirmed over the weekend that Solidigm is considering a US initial public offering (IPO) as soon as next year that could value the data-storage product maker at as much as US$100 billion ($128 billion). SK Hynix’s biggest holder SK Square Co tumbled more than 8%, while SK Inc, which controls SK Square, retreated more than 6%.

An IPO of Solidigm would add to the multiple layers of ownership within the group, deepening the pyramid ownership structure, according to the Korea Corporate Governance Forum, a non-profit of investment professionals, which in August urged SK Hynix to drop the plan. SK Hynix owns the NAND memory unit through US subsidiary AI Company, making Solidigm a so-called grandchild company.

“I would be watchful rather than alarmed,” said Jung In Yun, the chief executive officer of Fibonacci Asset Management Global. “A US listing could unlock Solidigm’s value and fund expansion, but SK Hynix shareholders would be giving up a portion of its future earnings.”

See also: TSMC affiliate plans second Singapore chip plant in Asia push

“The key is the valuation and the use of proceeds,” Yun said. “Selling a small stake at an attractive price could create value, while substantial dilution without a convincing investment return would be a concern.”

Shares of SK Hynix and other chipmakers, including Samsung Electronics Co, also came under pressure from broader risk-off mood after oil prices rose.

title: South Korea’s three-year yield rises to highest level since 2022
article:
(Sept 28): South Korea’s three-year yield rose to the highest level since November 2022 as the local bond market reopened after holidays, joining a global selloff as elevated oil prices stoked concern over inflation.

The yield jumped 11 basis points to 4.11%. Local markets were shut on Thursday and Friday, during which the longest-dated US bond yields climbed to the highest level in more than two decades.

“The fact that Korean yields are surging as well shows that this isn’t just a US issue, and it shows the market is growing concerned the Bank of Korea (BOK) will have to deliver more hikes,” said Kang Seungwon, a fixed-income analyst at NH Investment & Securities. A second straight Federal Reserve rate hike in October would most likely cement a Bank of Korea rate increase in November, Kang said.

Treasuries were lower in Asia on Monday, with bonds in Japan and Australia also falling as oil prices rallied after President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Korean bonds have struggled for most of the year as the ongoing war in the Middle East boosted oil prices, raising concerns about faster inflation in a country that relies heavily on imported energy. The BOK has already delivered back-to-back rate hikes as stronger-than-expected economic growth driven by an unprecedented semiconductor boom added to price pressures.

See also: Rising fuel costs drive up brewing costs in Asia, Heineken says

The BOK held a market review meeting on Monday to assess global financial conditions during the Sept 24-27 holidays. Authorities will closely monitor markets as volatility could expand, the central bank said in a statement released following the meeting.

title: Rising fuel costs drive up brewing costs in Asia, Heineken says
article:
(Sept 28): Rising fuel costs triggered by the Iran war are pushing up Heineken NV’s brewing costs in Asia, according to Asia-Pacific president Jacco van der Linden.

“We see that coming through in our input costs, predominantly in Asia,” he said in an interview with Bloomberg TV on Monday. “In Asia, we’re more dependent on oil coming from the Middle East and the reserves are somewhat smaller.”

The Dutch brewer is passing on around 70% to 80% of inflation to consumers while relying on more efficient productivity to absorb the rest, Van der Linden said.

“Input costs are rising, and therefore productivity — but also revenue management — are becoming more and more important to us,” he said.

The higher costs come as brewers globally grapple with consumers who are drinking less and whose tastes are shifting, including to healthier beverages. Heineken has lagged rivals AB InBev and Carlsberg A/S in turning business around after a post-Covid slump. Incoming chief executive officer Rafael Oliveira, the first outsider to lead Heineken, will inherit sluggish sales in Europe and the US when he takes the reins in October.

That makes growth in emerging markets increasingly important. Heineken is tapping rising demand in Asia, Africa and other developing economies to offset weakness in Europe and the Americas. Volumes jumped 13% in Asia-Pacific and 3.5% in Africa and the Middle East in the second quarter, while falling 4.1% in the Americas.

See also: Global funds end underweight position on China after four years

Heineken needs to keep investing in Asia, Africa and Latin America and pushing more premium products to counter weaker sales in its mature markets, according to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Ignacio Canals Polo. Vietnam and Mexico “show how the strategy can work,” he wrote in a Sept. 10 research note.

The company is focusing on key growth markets — particularly those in Asia, such as Vietnam, India and China, where consumers prefer lighter beers — Van der Linden said.

title: China may let Alibaba buy Nvidia’s RTX chips, Information reports
article:
(Sept 28): The Chinese government has signalled it may allow companies such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd and ByteDance Ltd to buy Nvidia Corp’s new RTX Pro 5500 chips, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently asked some companies to report on their plans to purchase the high-end graphics processor released this month, including how many and what they would use the product for, The Information said. The ministry told some of the firms it intends to approve the purchases, it reported.

Washington bars Nvidia’s most powerful accelerators from China, concerned they would propel the country’s AI efforts and aid the military of a geopolitical ally. The RTX Pro 5500, however, is a processor intended mainly for graphics and simulations, though it can also support artificial intelligence (AI) services. Unlike Nvidia’s top-of-the-line accelerators such as the GB300 series, it’s built on older-generation processes and is designed to provide workstation computation at scale.

While Chinese AI developers rely on Nvidia for training frontier large language models, they are grappling with a persistent shortage of capable AI chips. They often employ a mix of semiconductors from both foreign and local suppliers. On Monday, stocks in AI chip firms including Shanghai Biren Technology Co and Cambricon Technologies Corp fell on fears that an influx of foreign product may dent local demand.

“China has been pushing quite hard towards domestic chip self-sufficiency, so Beijing potentially allowing Alibaba and ByteDance to buy another Nvidia chip suggests pragmatism,” said Charu Chanana, the chief investment strategist of Saxo. “Domestic chips are improving quickly, but there are still gaps in performance, supply and the broader AI ecosystem that Nvidia can fill.”

The US administration recently lifted restrictions on some Nvidia chips, though the products tend to be older-generation chips that have been sold in small quantities.

See also: Bill Gates says Trump is wrong to hold out against AI safeguards

title: TSMC affiliate plans second Singapore chip plant in Asia push
article:
(Sept 28): A venture by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co’s smaller affiliate Vanguard International Semiconductor Corp is considering a second chipmaking plant in Singapore to meet growing demand.

VisionPower Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, a venture between Vanguard and NXP Semiconductors NV of the Netherlands, could make more advanced chips in the new facility than in its first plant in the city-state, Leuh Fang, chairman of Vanguard and the joint venture, said in an interview.

Rising demand for artificial intelligence services and the data centres to power them has led to global shortages of semiconductors, even with major producers such as TSMC constantly adding capacity. The boom has prompted Taiwanese manufacturers to venture abroad for new production plants, with Singapore among locations attracting global investment.

“The supply shortage will last for a while,” Fang said. “We should’ve built two plants together here.”

VSMC on Monday inaugurated its first Singapore chip plant, in the eastern part of the country. Construction of the facility started in late 2024, with the company estimating it will invest US$7.8 billion ($9.97 billion). Fang declined to estimate the cost of the potential second plant.

“It’s still too early to talk about budget because we haven’t decided on what type of technologies to be used,” he said. “Different technologies will greatly affect total size of investment.”

See also: SK Hynix shares fall as subsidiary Solidigm’s potential US IPO sours mood

title: Trump says he’s ‘very seriously’ looking at diesel export ban
article:
(Sept 28): US President Donald Trump said he is still looking “very seriously” at implementing a US ban on diesel exports to combat high prices, even as others in his administration continue to focus on other possible steps.

“That can oftentimes lead to a little bit of an increase on gasoline for cars, so we’re looking at it very seriously — we may do it,” Trump told a Fox News reporter on Sunday while attending the Presidents Cup golf tournament final near Chicago.

Several farm-state lawmakers have urged Trump to limit US diesel exports during the peak of the fall harvest season, as global fuel markets reel from the disruption to flows in the critical Strait of Hormuz and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. The US has emerged as the supplier of last resort to the world, with diesel exports surging to a weekly record near two million barrels a day last month.

National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have been analysing the ramifications of a potential short-term ban on US diesel exports over the last week, underscoring the seriousness of the administration’s consideration of the idea.

Oil chief executive officers and industry groups have pushed instead for suspending the federal diesel excise tax, saying it would ease prices without the drawbacks of an export ban. But that’s been met with internal debate about how to waive the tax — especially with the House of Representatives in a pre-election recess.

Diesel powers farm equipment, freight trains, trucks and delivery vans. US retail prices hit a record last week and are averaging about US$6.50 a gallon, adding to voter anxiety over living costs before November’s midterm elections.

See also: Oil rises as Iran says it won’t soften Strait of Hormuz demands

Energy Secretary Chris Wright said last week that the administration is working with refiners on voluntary export curbs as an alternative to a government-imposed ban.

Some companies are already adding contractual protections in the event a pause on diesel shipments overseas prevents deliveries to foreign buyers, people with knowledge of the situation told Bloomberg News last Friday.

In the event of a ban, US diesel prices would be widely expected to plummet, at least in the short run. A halt would leave America’s allies, including Brazil and the UK, urgently needing to secure fuel.

title: Bill Gates says Trump is wrong to hold out against AI safeguards
article:
(Sept 28): Microsoft Corp co-founder Bill Gates said government safeguards against potentially catastrophic artificial intelligence (AI) risks won’t hamper the US in its competition with China, contrasting with President Donald Trump’s largely hands-off approach.

“Certainly, all countries should want the safeguards in place,” Gates said in an interview with NBC’s Meet the Press. “So anyone that says, ‘Well, you know, China won’t put these safeguards in place’ — I totally disagree with that.”

Gates is among the tech leaders weighing in as the rapidly advancing technology stokes debate about AI safety, including warnings by some that it will put humanity at risk. In an interview excerpt released last week, Gates told NBC that AI is a powerful enough tool to “cause a billion deaths”.

Faced with low approval ratings as the Republicans fight to retain control of Congress in elections in November, Trump has portrayed warnings of existential AI risks as a hoax that threatens US innovation and plays into China’s hands.

“It’s not a hoax at all,” Gates said, when asked about Trump’s remarks.

He said he expects China to join in supporting AI safety because it doesn’t want to be a target of attacks. Trump, he argued, might shift his stance “after he hears from me and other people — including that this does not handicap us in whatever he thinks the nation-state race is.”

See also: From geisha face paint to servers, Sakai Chemical emerges as AI linchpin

Gates previously argued in an essay in August that bad actors could use increasingly powerful AI tools for cyberattacks, fraud, disinformation and other forms of large-scale harm against hospitals, financial institutions, power grids and government systems.

A kill switch — the idea of ensuring that humans retain the ability to stop or restrict a powerful AI model if it begins behaving dangerously — is “not enough” and can’t replace oversight at earlier stages, Gates told NBC.

“We do need to monitor any sophisticated model and record exactly what’s being done,” he said. “The US ought to make sure this is done. China will want to do this.”

title: Fastest megawatt is the winning megawatt: Tan See Leng
article:
As energy becomes increasingly key to attracting investments, it is imperative for Singapore to keep up with demand in a timely manner, says Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) Dr Tan See Leng.

“In many respects, the fastest megawatt is the winning megawatt,” remarks Tan, who was speaking at the groundbreaking of Singapore’s first gas-fired power plant with an integrated battery energy storage system (BESS). “We must therefore continue investing in new generation capacity ahead of demand so that Singapore can seize new investment opportunities and support our future growth.”

To be built on Jurong Island at a cost of $1.2 billion by PacificLight Power subsidiary PLM Power, the new plant has a generation capacity of 670MW and is capable of co-firing with hydrogen up to 30% by volume from the outset, with the goal of transitioning to 100% hydrogen in the future.

Meanwhile, the plant’s 80MW BESS supports dynamic energy management and strengthens grid resiliency by helping to align electricity supply with demand, with a response time of two seconds.

Scheduled to commence operations in 2029, PacificLight says that the facility will be Singapore’s largest and most efficient single generating unit, capable of powering the needs of 1.2 million four-room flats.

“Singapore’s peak electricity demand is projected to grow at a faster pace in the coming years, driven by advanced manufacturing, digital economy and transport electrification,” says Tan. He adds that the situation is “not unique” to Singapore, with other countries also “racing to secure” the energy capacity required to support new economic growth.

See also: Homegrown EGP Energy eyes overseas expansion to power growth as shares climb after IPO

The right to build, own and operate the plant was awarded to PacificLight in January 2025 by the Energy Market Authority (EMA). The new plant will add to PacificLight’s existing 830MW combined gas-cycle turbine facility and its 100MW fast start ancillary services facility, both of which are also located on Jurong Island.

"This investment also aligns with Singapore's vision for Jurong Island's continued transformation as a hub for sustainable energy and advanced industries," says PacificLight chairman Emmanuel Rubio. "That vision reinforces the importance of investing in infrastructure that not only meets today's needs but is also adaptable to the energy systems of tomorrow."

title: US, China release product lists for US$30 bil tariff deal
article:
(Sept 28): The US and China detailed a plan to cut tariffs on about US$30 billion ($96 billion) of imports from each country, as the superpower rivals take steps to steady ties following a summit between leaders Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.

The list for goods entering the US contains 77 entries, including fireworks, household products, sporting equipment and toys, according to documents published by both governments.

They also listed 1,619 goods set to potentially enter China, such as meat, seafood, dairy products, grains, coal, timber and medical equipment.

The expected tariff relief for US$60 billion in bilateral trade was one of the most tangible outcomes of Xi’s state visit to Washington last week, even though the amount is a fraction of the US$415 billion in total goods exchanged between the world’s largest economies last year.

The two sides extended their trade truce until January as they pursue a broader agreement ahead of two more expected meetings between Trump and Xi this year. With major disputes over export controls and Taiwan unresolved, non-sensitive trade has emerged as one area where agreements remain possible.

Shares of some Chinese appliance makers rose after details of the tariff cuts emerged, with Joyoung Co jumping by the 10% limit in Shenzhen and Bear Electric Appliance up as much as 9.5%.

See also: Xi seizes Trump detente to seek lasting gains on trade, Taiwan

China said the tariff reductions would take place simultaneously after fulfilling procedures required in domestic law.

“This arrangement will help to further stabilise China-US economic and trade relations and create favourable conditions for China’s exports of relevant products to the US,” the Chinese Commerce Ministry said.

About 90% of the products covered by the reciprocal arrangement would have their tariffs reduced to most-favoured-nation rates, according to a statement.

See also: Trump-Xi summit goes big on pomp but small on substance

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer described the selected products as non-sensitive goods that could qualify for more favourable tariff treatment. He said the recommendations would improve access for US agricultural products and medical devices while lowering barriers on Chinese household goods and toys.

“President Trump is unlocking improved market access for about 30% of US exports to China, while benefiting consumers with imports from China of household goods, toys, and other products that the United States generally does not import from other countries,” Greer said.

Beijing said tariffs on coal imported from the US would be included in the framework, a step it said would support Chinese purchases in 2027 and 2028. The White House previously said China agreed to import at least 10 million tonnes of coal from the US next year and again in 2028.

Key grains, including wheat, corn and sorghum, are among the agricultural exports destined for a tariff cut.

That could help China make progress toward a goal to buy at least US$17 billion in US agricultural products annually through 2028, in addition to a commitment to buy 25 million tonnes of soybeans per year. Progress towards the US$17 billion goal has been slow since it was announced by the Trump administration after the last leaders’ summit in May, with traders looking to potential tariff cuts from the meeting in Washington DC to spark a wave of new buying.

Agricultural purchases are often seen as the low hanging fruit of any trade deal between the US and China, less complicated than more sensitive issues such as chip technology or artificial intelligence. A new Agricultural Working Group will be established between the two countries following the summit, according to China’s Commerce Ministry, with an inaugural meeting set to take place by the end of 2026.

title: Bonds drop with stocks as Iran tensions boost oil
article:
(Sept 18): Bonds and stocks dropped after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, denting some of the optimism that lifted markets late last week. The dollar strengthened, while precious metals sold off.

Shorter-maturity Treasuries led losses, with the rate-sensitive two-year yield climbing five basis points to 4.90%, as elevated energy costs kept pressure on the Federal Reserve (Fed) to raise interest rates to combat inflation. The benchmark 10-year yield advanced four basis points, erasing Friday’s decline that was spurred by expectations US and Iranian negotiators were exploring a phased deal that would reopen the vital waterway.

Brent crude gained 1.8% to about US$106 a barrel after Iran said it wouldn’t soften its demands and stuck to a seven-day proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Gold dropped 1.9% to about US$4,200 an ounce and silver lost more than 3% to about US$62 an ounce as prospects of higher rates weighed on the non-yielding metals.

MSCI’s index of Asian stocks slipped 0.5%, with benchmark equity gauges in mainland China and South Korea dropping more than 2%. Futures for the Nasdaq 100 Index fell 0.7%.

Oil remains a key driver for markets as elevated energy costs add to inflation pressures and bolster expectations for further rate increases. Last week, the average yield on a gauge of global bonds climbed above 4% for the first time since 2007, raising concerns that higher borrowing costs may eventually weigh on the economy and on company earnings. Some reprieve came Friday amid hopes for US-Iran talks to ease tensions in the Middle East and revive the transport of oil and gas through Hormuz.

“Investors were once again disappointed by the lack of diplomatic progress,” said Rajeev De Mello, senior macro portfolio manager at Gama Asset Management. “Hopes that these discussions would help de-escalate the Middle East conflict and pave the way for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz were dashed.”

See also: House of cards in bonds

The conditions Iran wants are something Washington might have agreed to about a year ago, Trump told Axios in an interview on Sunday, saying that Tehran has overplayed its hand. The US president added that he expects negotiations to resume this week even though he rejected Iran’s latest proposal, Axios reported.

Tensions in the Middle East have boosted oil prices by about 75% this year.

Brent’s so-called prompt spread — the difference between its two nearest contracts — expanded to about US$7.75 a barrel in backwardation, up from about US$4 a week ago. The widening spread — with November’s price at a premium to December’s — points to elevated concerns about near-term tightness.

See also: Bonds stabilise as oil declines, stocks edge up

Elsewhere, the pound steadied as UK police investigated a potential terrorism incident after five men were arrested near an air base used in US strikes on Iran. Trump said the suspects were “looking to do big damage” to the facility.

In tariff-related news, the US released details of a plan to slash tariffs on roughly US$30 billion (RM122.54 billion) of imported goods on each side following a summit between Trump and Xi Jinping. Chinese chip stocks dropped after a report that the nation may allow purchases of Nvidia Corp’s new chips.

Government bonds in Japan, Australia and New Zealand fell along with Treasuries.

The Middle East gridlock is “likely to remain the market’s focus” until the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge and US jobs report arrive later this week, said Prashant Newnaha, senior Asia-Pacific rates strategist at TD Securities in Singapore.

Several Fed officials have pointed to resilient economic growth and a strong labour market as reasons further tightening may be needed. Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack said those factors, along with concerns about government debt, are helping drive long-term Treasury yields higher.

Traders are fully pricing at least one more 25-basis-point hike by year-end after the central bank raised borrowing costs this month for the first time since 2023.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent struck a more dovish tone, saying policymakers should keep an “open mind” on rates as productivity gains from artificial intelligence and deregulation may help contain inflation.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

“As long as the Iran conflict persists, markets will face the prospects of higher inflation, rate hikes, and tighter financial conditions,” said Vey-Sern Ling, a managing director at Union Bancaire Privee. “But investors should watch for buying opportunities with a longer-term view, given the depressed valuations this time, supported by surging AI-driven earnings.”

Some of the main moves in markets:
• The euro was little changed at US$1.1386
• The Japanese yen fell 0.3% to 157.80 per dollar
• The offshore yuan was little changed at 6.7170 per dollar
• The yield on 10-year Treasuries advanced four basis points to 5.20%

title: From geisha face paint to servers, Sakai Chemical emerges as AI linchpin
article:
(Sept 28): Sakai Chemical Industry Co’s century-old expertise in producing fine powders for face makeup used by geisha is finding a lucrative new use — powering the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

Production capacity is quickly filling up at the Osaka-based company, which provides raw materials for capacitors necessary in AI data centres. Until recently, such production was a side business for Sakai Chemical, which has spent decades perfecting the production of ultra-fine and uniform particles — whether for safe, lead-free base material for traditional Japanese face powders, or for chemical compounds that store big electrical charges inside tiny components in servers.

The last year has transformed Sakai Chemical into a little-known tech supply chain linchpin. The company’s now calculating how much more production capability it needs to add, according to its president Toshiyuki Yagura.

A double-digit increase in manufacturing capacity is likely, according to Yagura. Advanced multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) makers — such as clients Murata Manufacturing Co and Taiyo Yuden Co — raise their order forecasts at every meeting, he said. Sakai Chemical will make a decision regarding capex by March, he added.

“I didn’t think demand would grow this fast, and that’s all because of AI,” Yagura said in an interview, adding that he fields wistful jokes about the possibility of Sakai Chemical building facilities next to MLCC makers’ factories. The pace of AI-led momentum has eased somewhat, but he said the boom will likely last through 2027 at least.

Last quarter, Sakai Chemical’s electronics materials segment profit rose 22%, even as company-wide operating profit fell 10%, hurt by weak demand for building materials in Japan and changing trends in the sunscreen market. Electronics materials are now the company’s largest profit generator, surpassing its mainstay plastic additives business. The company’s stock price is up about 15% this year.

See also: Microsoft abandons personal AI chatbot race with Copilot reboot

The 108-year-old company started out by supplying high-purity zinc oxide as a safe alternative to the white lead historically used in the iconic makeup of geisha and kabuki entertainers. The older form of makeup provided a smooth, brilliant and long-lasting white finish, but caused chronic lead poisoning in Japan’s artist class. Sakai Chemical offered a safe material that offered white, opaque coverage that spread easily over the skin. From makeup, Sakai Chemical soon expanded into materials used in products ranging from sunscreens and car tyres to plastics and barium compounds.

The AI spending rush has put a spotlight on the company’s expertise in barium titanate, a critical chemical compound needed to make MLCCs — tiny components that regulate power flow in electronics. High-end capacitors used in AI servers need to be made from ultra-fine, uniform and high-purity barium titanate particles.

Sakai Chemical has been supplying the material for decades, but sales only began surging late last year, when annual orders for some products doubled as the AI infrastructure boom fuelled demand.

See also: When AI writes its own audit trail

While MLCC manufacturers also make the ingredient by mixing, firing and grinding barium and titanium compounds, they turn to Sakai Chemical for the materials needed to make capacitors for AI servers, according to Yagura. To make its ultra-pure powder, Sakai Chemical makes the compounds react in a liquid solution while exposing them to high temperature and pressure — a difficult process that requires precise control of multiple variables.

Despite high demand and insufficient capacity, the company has no plans to raise prices of its MLCC particles beyond what’s required to cover higher input costs, according to Yagura. That’s even as he acknowledges such reluctance weighs on corporate value.

“We are modest but proud of doing things right,” Yagura said.

Chinese manufacturers are spending heavily to catch up in chips, semiconductor materials and MLCCs. While Chinese companies’ market presence is growing in electronic materials, Japanese manufacturers retain an edge in consistency, Yagura said.

“Chinese makers may be able to show off their best samples out of their labs, but consistently delivering products of reliable quality is something Japan excels at,” he said.

title: Global funds end underweight position on China after four years
article:
(Sept 28): Global fund managers are dialing back their long-running retreat from Chinese stocks, drawn by AI prospects and favourable valuations.

Of nearly 2,800 global funds analysed by Bank of America, active long-only funds have, on average, moved to a “benchmark-neutral” weighting on China starting June, ending a four-year run of being “underweight,” according to its strategist Nigel Tupper. The funds collectively manage $562 billion in Chinese stocks.

The shift shows funds are encouraged by attractive valuations and improving profit outlooks in growth sectors like artificial intelligence. While it doesn’t necessarily signal a broad bullish turn, it indicates managers are largely done cutting their exposure, removing a major hurdle for the market’s recovery.

“Selling pressure is nearing a floor, shifting investor focus from positioning to earnings delivery,” Gary Tan, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, said, adding his firm is selectively adding Chinese stocks. “China does not need global investors to turn outright bullish for the market backdrop to improve; it may simply need them to stop cutting exposure.”

Other flow data point to a similar direction. Exchange-traded funds focused on China and Hong Kong drew US$19 million in August after US$1.94 billion of outflows in July, according to Bloomberg Intelligence’s (BI) data. Meanwhile, outflows from emerging-market funds that exclude China have been rising.

See also: Geely to buy 30% stake in Rival Nio’s battery-swapping unit

“China’s systematic ETF underweight is likely approaching a floor after the sharpest allocation reduction among major emerging markets,” said BI analyst Rebecca Sin. “The forces creating China’s underweight have started to lose momentum.”

Valuations may be helping. The MSCI China Index is trading at about 10.2 times 12-month forward earnings, below its 10-year average of 11.7 times.

See also: US releases product lists for US$30 bil China tariff deal

Investors are also finding improving earnings in parts of the market tied to Beijing’s technology ambitions. Shanghai-listed companies posted a 17.6% rise in first-half net income, according to Shanghai Securities News, driven by tech hardware and new-economy companies even as property and consumer industries lagged.

That divergence also means China’s market recovery remains uneven. The CSI 300 has fallen about 11% this quarter, and investors remain selective about where they put money.

“You buy the future of China,” Herald van der Linde, head of equity strategy for Asia Pacific at HSBC Holdings Plc, said, citing hardware technology and biopharma as preferred sectors. Consumer industries and real estate are “the past of China.”

title: Geely to buy 30% stake in Rival Nio’s battery-swapping unit
article:
(Sept 28): Zhejiang Geely Holding Group Co will buy a 30% stake in rival electric carmaker Nio Inc’s battery swapping unit for 640 million yuan (US$95 million), providing support for a cash intensive technology that Nio has been spearheading.

Geely will also include 100% equity interest of a battery swapping subsidiary as well as 640 million yuan in cash for the stake in Nio Power. The deal values Nio Power at 16 billion yuan, according to a statement on Monday.

The partnership comes as Nio continues to look for ways to further commercialise its battery swapping business. The technology is a unique selling point for its electric vehicles where drivers can replace a depleted battery with a charged one in a few minutes, but requires heavy investment and operational costs to build and maintain swapping stations. Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd invested 2.5 billion yuan into Nio Power last year in a collaboration to build out a battery swapping network across China.

title: HSBC makes big push for affluent clients in India to fuel growth
article:
(Sept 28): HSBC Holdings plc is aiming to challenge India’s private-sector banks, betting that the country’s swelling pool of affluent customers and globally connected citizens can fuel its next phase of growth as it pushes deeper into smaller cities.

The London-based lender is doubling down in the world’s fastest-growing major economy across three areas — wealth, transaction banking and what Hitendra Dave, HSBC’s India chief executive officer, calls “globality”, — using its international network to cater to clients whose businesses and wealth span borders.

“Our ambition is to become one of the top four or five private banks in India by 2030,” the Mumbai-based executive said in an interview, referring to the wealth management business.

The growth drive puts HSBC in more direct competition with larger local rivals including ICICI Bank Ltd and Kotak Mahindra Ltd for a slice of India’s fast-expanding wealth pool. Still, the market is tricky to navigate as domestic banks are scaling up while firms founded by senior bankers are fighting for clients and talent, helping drive pay for relationship managers to record highs.

HSBC, Standard Chartered plc and Barclays plc are among a relatively small group of foreign banks building out their wealth management businesses in India, even as some global lenders have pulled back. Citigroup Inc sold its Indian consumer banking unit to Axis Bank Ltd, while Kotak agreed this year to acquire Deutsche Bank AG’s retail and wealth management businesses in India. Foreign lenders also face tighter restrictions on opening branches than their domestic rivals, making it harder to build nationwide networks.

The UK lender’s push comes as group chief executive officer Georges Elhedery said in a recent interview that the bank plans to increase investments in India, with a growing focus on affluent customers.

See also: ANZ bankers in Hong Kong, Singapore, Australia to exit in revamp — Bloomberg

The firm plans to expand to 46 branches across 34 cities in India over the next two years, from 34 branches currently, taking it further in smaller places. New locations include Bhubaneswar in the east, Rajkot in the west, Jalandhar in the north and Mysuru in the south. Standard Chartered has the largest network among foreign banks in the country, with 80 branches.

“We are building a wealth franchise beyond India’s metro cities,” said Dave, pointing to the growing number of wealthy individuals in smaller centres. HSBC’s private bank generally targets customers with at least US$2 million (RM8.17 million) in investable assets.

Dave described the next generation of Indian wealth as increasingly ‘global’, as more Indians study and work overseas, build international businesses and invest globally. “We can be especially valuable to customers whose financial lives, businesses and wealth cross borders,” he said.

See also: DBS seeks better AI returns by matching models to tasks

The firm’s expansion is already paying dividends. HSBC recently emerged as the biggest lender to India’s vast diaspora under a special foreign-exchange swap programme, disbursing US$10.9 billion from GIFT City in three months. ICICI Bank ranked second with US$8.4 billion.

HSBC is also using premium credit cards and large-ticket mortgages to deepen relationships with wealthy customers. Annual fees on its premium cards can run as high as 110,000 rupees (US$1,147 or RM4,685), while its mortgage book has tripled over the past four years.

Outstanding mortgages rose 25% from a year earlier to 257 billion rupees as of March 31, according to the bank as it focused on larger loans for premium homes. Transaction banking is another pillar of the strategy, with the lender helping companies process payroll, make foreign-exchange payments, distribute dividends and manage liquidity, Dave said.

title: CDL shares swoon to six-week low after $6 bil divestment target news
article:
Shares in City Developments (CDL) fell at open from $8.25 to an intra-day low of $7.74 before recovering to $7.91 as at 10.08am on Sept 28. The property group’s stock swooned following its pre-market announcement that it would divest $6 billion of assets while deploying $5 billion into Singapore, China, Japan and other markets.

CDL shares erased around six weeks’ worth of gains after the group released the outcome of its year-long strategic review, which group CEO Sherman Kwek first announced in February.

CDL is the day’s biggest loser, sinking the most out of the 30-stock Straits Times Index bellwether index as at 10am on Sept 28.

CDL is targeting $6 billion of divestments across the residential, commercial, hospitality and living sectors while deploying $5 billion of growth capital across the four sectors.

Nearly half (45%) of the targeted asset divestment mix will come from commercial properties. Hospitality assets are targeted to make up 30% of divestments, while legacy residential and other sectors will make up one-fifth of the $6 billion target and living sector assets will make up 5%.

See also: CDL targets $6 bil of divestments, aims to deploy $5 bil mostly in Singapore

Under a three-year refreshed strategy named GET+, CDL will also optimise its global hospitality portfolio of 165 hotels with around 48,000 rooms, including 88 owned hotels. Of these, 54 hotels (including two opening in the next 12 months) are directly held by CDL and valued at approximately $8.6 billion.

CDL says it will retain core assets but target approximately $1.8 billion of hotel divestments through FY2029, representing 30% of its $6 billion divestment target.

Singapore will remain the principal market for new investments, according to CDL. The group has shared a 60%-30%-10% breakdown for new investments across Singapore, China and Japan, and other markets respectively.

See also: Incredible Holdings seeks to be placed under judicial management

In addition to the divestment proceeds, the group expects more than $6 billion of projected cash inflows through to FY2029 from property development sales, supported by future cash collections from contracted sales and its existing development pipeline.

CDL will also establish a dedicated fund management entity, as the group aims to double assets under management (AUM) from $5 billion as of June 30 to $10 billion by FY2029.

The group says the fund management platform will create “a proprietary pipeline of opportunities” that can be seeded from CDL’s portfolio or new acquisitions and scaled with third-party capital.

Together, the group’s “four targeted measurable outcomes” include $1 billion in patmi to be realised from divestment gains, a net gearing target of around 55% by FY2029, a 35% or higher dividend payout ratio on reported patmi annually and $10 billion in AUM.

CDL will hold a briefing for media and analysts later today.

CDL shares closed 0.5% higher at $8.26 on Sept 25. CDL shares had surged past $10 in February in the lead up to the release of its FY2025 results.

title: Oil, AI demand give ringgit room to rally, strategists say
article:
(Sept 28): The Malaysian ringgit may be poised for gains as higher oil prices and the artificial-intelligence boom provide tailwinds for the currency, strategists say.

While the ringgit has declined 1.2% in September, lagging all Asian peers, MUFG Bank expects it to strengthen to 4.03 per dollar by year-end. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp sees it at 4.0.

The ringgit closed 0.3% higher at 4.0738 per dollar on Friday.

A renewed climb in oil prices may bolster revenues for the energy exporting country, while Malaysia’s growing role in the AI supply chain gives it exposure to rising demand for semiconductors. With the political risk premium around some state elections also fading, strategists expect the ringgit to resume its advance.

“We could see a relief rally in the ringgit towards the year-end as macro environment concerns ease,” said Jeff Ng, head of Asia macro strategy at Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp in Singapore. “Malaysia’s overall fundamentals are still positive,” given its energy and electronic exports, as well as linkages to a stronger Chinese yuan, he said.

See also: Penang E&E players face capacity crunch amid influx of orders

The country’s exports have surged more than 35% in each of the five months through August, boosted by shipments of electronic products including semiconductors. Export growth averaged about 6.7% in 2025. Malaysia is now one of the world’s four largest net exporters of AI-related hardware, alongside South Korea, Taiwan and Thailand, according to the International Monetary Fund.

“Malaysia’s electronics trade surplus has been able to help offset the higher oil import bill,” said Lloyd Chan, a foreign-exchange strategist at MUFG in Singapore. “We see scope for ringgit strength,” supported by attractive sovereign bond and ringgit valuations, he added.

The local currency’s real effective exchange rate is around 2% below the 20-year average, according to data from the Bank for International Settlements. Continued bond inflows may help underpin the ringgit.

See also: UWC’s downturn bet puts it in pole position for semiconductor front-end boom

Investors will be watching the S&P Malaysia manufacturing PMI print for September due Thursday for further signs of economic expansion, as the region continues to grapple with the fallout from the Middle East. Still, Malaysia may be better placed than some peers to weather higher energy costs as one of the world’s top exporters of liquefied natural gas.

“Malaysia has been on the right side of the terms-of-trade story throughout the year,” and is best-positioned to benefit from AI investment and higher energy prices, Goldman Sachs Group Inc strategists including Danny Suwanapruti wrote in a note on Sept 18. With the central bank turning slightly more hawkish, “the conditions are in place for ringgit to outperform,” they said, recommending a long ringgit/baht trade.

title: Low family controlling Hafary Holdings tables 64 cents privatisation offer
article:
The Low family controlling Hafary Holdings is making an offer of 64 cents per share to privatise the company.

They will not revise the offer, which is made via a vehicle called 23 Capital.

Together with an entity called Hap Seng Investment Holdings, the concerted parties already control 89.96% of the company, which is a supplier of building materials.

The offer of 64 cents is a premium of around 4.9% over the last transacted price per share on Sept 25.

As of June 30, Hafary's net asset value was 35.2 cents per share.

See also: Privatisation offer for Low Keng Huat raised to 78 cents per share

In the most recent half year ended June, the company reported earnings of $10.2 million, down 22.2% y-o-y. Revenue in the same period was down 10.5% to $122.7 million.

According to the offerors, Hafary has not raised capital from the market in the last decade and does not see itself doing so in the foreseeable future, as it can tap bank borrowings.

title: CDL targets $6 bil of divestments, aims to deploy $5 bil mostly in Singapore
article:
City Developments (CDL) is targeting $6 billion of divestments across the residential, commercial, hospitality and living sectors while deploying $5 billion of growth capital across the four sectors, following its strategic review.

Nearly half (45%) of the targeted asset divestment mix will come from commercial properties. Singapore will remain the principal market for new investments, says CDL in a Sept 28 announcement.

The group has shared a 60%, 30% and 10% breakdown for new investments across Singapore, China and Japan, and other markets respectively.

Under a three-year refreshed strategy named GET+, CDL will also optimise its global hospitality portfolio of 165 hotels with around 48,000 rooms, including 88 owned hotels. Of these, 54 hotels (including two opening in the next 12 months) are directly held by CDL and valued at approximately $8.6 billion.

CDL says it will retain core assets but target approximately $1.8 billion of hotel divestments through FY2029, representing 30% of its $6 billion divestment target.

See also: Incredible Holdings seeks to be placed under judicial management

In addition to the divestment proceeds, the group expects more than $6 billion of projected cash inflows through to FY2029 from property development sales, supported by future cash collections from contracted sales and its existing development pipeline.

CDL will also establish a dedicated fund management entity, as the group aims to double assets under management (AUM) from $5 billion as of June 30 to $10 billion by FY2029.

See also: Incredible Holdings’ independent director interviewed by CAD, MAS (update)

Together, the group’s “four targeted measurable outcomes” include $1 billion in patmi to be realised from divestment gains, a net gearing target of around 55% by FY2029, a 35% or higher dividend payout ratio on reported patmi annually and $10 billion in AUM.

CDL’s gearing rose to 75% at June 30, from 71% six months prior. CDL management attributed this to the two government land sales (GLS) sites it acquired at Tanjong Rhu Road and Peck Hay Road over the period.

Kwek Leng Beng, executive chairman of CDL, says: “For over six decades, CDL has built a strong and diversified real estate and hospitality portfolio supported by deep capabilities and quality assets. The strategic review builds on these strengths, while sharpening our priorities and setting a clear direction for the group.”

Sherman Kwek, group CEO of CDL, says: “GET+ marks our next chapter of value creation, with a three-year execution roadmap marked by a sharper focus around where we deploy capital, how we manage our portfolio and where we can unlock value. Through the 3-4-5-6 roadmap and measurable outcomes, we have provided greater accountability for what we need to deliver and our unwavering focus will be on strong execution as we work to strengthen our balance sheet, improve capital productivity and build a higher-quality earnings base to maximise shareholder value.”

CDL will hold a briefing for media and analysts later today.

The junior Kwek first announced the review on Feb 27 during the group’s results presentation for FY2025 ended Dec 31, 2025. He added that the group had engaged a global advisory firm, later revealed to be Teneo, to spearhead the review.

At the group’s 1HFY2026 results briefing in August, the junior Kwek said the review will include a “very concrete plan” that was backed by assets and numbers to lower its gearing to a level that he thinks everybody “should be very happy with”.

CDL shares closed 0.5% higher at $8.26 on Sept 25. CDL shares had surged past $10 in February in the lead up to the release of its FY2025 results.

title: Stoneweg Europe Stapled Trust proposes to internalise manager and operating platform
article:
Stoneweg Europe Stapled Trust is proposing to internalise the REIT manager, trustee-manager of the business trust and the pan-European logistics and light-industrial platform that manages SERT’s assets and selected third-party asset management contracts.

This follows an Aug 13 announcement where SERT said it was in discussions with its sponsor, SWI Group, regarding “a range of initiatives aimed at enhancing long-term value for stapled securityholders” including a proposed internalisation of the REIT manager and trustee-manager.

In SERT’s Sept 28 announcement, the trust says the transaction will create a platform with EUR3.2 billion ($4.7 billion) of assets under management (AUM), including SERT’s existing EUR2.3 billion portfolio and third-party asset management contracts totalling EUR820 million.

Along with the proposed internalisation, SERT will enter into two strategic cooperation agreements with with sponsor, SWI Group, which owns a 28% stake in SERT’s stapled securities and wholly owns the manager and property manager.

Operating as an independent and internally manager platform will allow SERT to benefit from “exclusive logistics and light industrial investment rights across Europe and, through these agreements, preferred access to SWI Group’s specialist data centre capabilities and opportunities,” says the trust.

The purchase consideration for the proposed internalisation is EUR114 million and the effective consideration is EUR94 million. Both figures exclude the co-investment stakes related to third-party asset management contracts. The difference reflects a benefit arising from the 40 million subscription securities issued to SWI Group at EUR2 per security, which is a 33% premium to the volume-weighted average trading price of around EUR1.50 as at Sept 24.

See also: Keppel REIT to divest T Tower at agreed property value of 348.8 bil won

The EUR2 issue price only applies to the one-off subscription by SWI and does not constitute a capital raise from existing securityholders.

The proposed internalisation will be funded through EUR80 million from SWI Group’s subscription for 40 million new SERT stapled securities and up to EUR34 million in cash payable by the trust. A further EUR8.4 million in cash may be paid for co-investment stakes linked to third-party asset management contracts that transfer to SERT by completion.

See also: MLT to divest property in Shanghai, China for RMB323 mil, extends lease at 201 Keppel Road for another nine months

The proposed internalisation will bring together 100 employees across 10 European jurisdictions and Singapore, who currently manage SERT’s 96 assets.

According to the managers, the proposed internalisation is expected to be accretive to SERT’s distribution per stapled security (DPS) by 5.9%, or 14.18 Euro cents on an FY2025 pro forma basis, up from 13.39 Euro cents.

The accretion is supported by earnings generated by the acquired management and operating platform, including other institutional asset management contracts and the EUR20 million adjustment to the consideration from SWI Group’s subscription.

SERT also noted other benefits including its securityholders benefitting from its platform earnings and future growth, noting a net uplift to distributable income of EUR10.1 million based on FY2025 fees paid to the sponsor.

Third-party asset management contracts, which generate recurring fee income, also create a broader earnings platform, while the agreements with sponsor SWI Group preserves SERT’s access to “future growth opportunities”.

Lim Swe Guan, chair and non-independent non-executive director of the manager, called the proposed internalisation a “landmark transaction” and a “deliberate step toward building a resilient, transparent and sustainably managed platform that delivers superior risk-adjusted returns to our securityholders over time”.

Max-Hervé George, founder & CEO of SWI Group added that the internalisation is a “milestone that cements its position as our flagship European logistics and light industrial vehicle – independently managed while remaining strategically connected to our global network, while SWI Group's team efforts will be concentrating on digital infrastructure.”

Jaume Sabater, founder & CEO of Stoneweg Group noted that the transaction marked a “natural evolution” of the REIT and sponsor’s partnership and said SWI Group will remain a long-term strategic investor of the trust.

“SERT is building on a strong foundation forged over nine years of proven track record and demonstrated resilience. Its long-term business performance is anchored by the REIT, which continues to deliver stable and growing distributions to securityholders, while the business trust and earnings from the acquired asset management platform provide additional sources of growth beyond the core portfolio,” says Simon Garing, CEO of the manager.

“Our two strategic cooperation agreements with SWI Group complement the proposed internalisation by preserving strategic access to logistics and data centre opportunities, maintaining SERT's independence as a fully internally managed platform and supporting continued growth in the logistics, light industrial and digital infrastructure sectors,” he adds.

The proposed internalisation and strategic cooperation agreements are subject to regulatory approvals, securityholders' approval at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) and other customary closing conditions. A circular together with a notice of the EGM will be issued, says SERT.

Units in SERT closed 5 Euro cents lower or 3.36% down at EUR1.44 while its SGD counter closed 7 cents lower or 3.23% down at $2.10 on Sept 25.

title: Mainboard-listed Oiltek submits application for Bursa Malaysia listing
article:
In a bourse filing on Sept 28, Mainboard-listed Oiltek International has announced that it has submitted an application for a secondary listing on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia on Sept 25. The application has been submitted by M & A Securities, Oiltek’s principal advisor, to the Securities Commission (SC) Malaysia.

First announced in July 2025, the secondary listing will comprise a public offering and a private placement of new shares. In addition, there will be a private placement for existing shares. The private placements are for Bumiputera investors approved by Malaysia’s Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry.

The final structure, size and issue/offer price of the new listing will be determined at a later date and will be announced in due course, says Oiltek. The listing will remain subject to, among others, the approvals of the SC, Bursa Securities, Bank Negara Malaysia, MITI and such other relevant authorities as may be required.

Upon receiving approval by the relevant authorities for the new listing, Oiltek will be convening an EGM to seek shareholders approval for constitution amendment, a proposed bonus shares issue for entitled shareholders and new shares issue for the Malaysian listing.

The company reported a decrease in net profit after tax (npat) of 6.9% y-o-y to RM13.2 ($4.15) million for 1HFY2026 ended June 30, with RM99.2 million in revenue, down 1.6% y-o-y from the previous corresponding period.

Shares in Oiltek closed at $1.25 on Sept 25. Ytd, the stock is up 78%.

title: Great Eastern Holdings appoints former ComfortDelGro director to its board
article:
Great Eastern Holdings has appointed Adeline Sum Wai Fun as an non-executive and independent director of the board.

Sum, whose appointment will take effect from Oct 1, will also be appointed as a member of Great Eastern’s audit committee on the same day.

According to the insurer, Sum possesses the “requisite experience and expertise” which would enable her to contribute to the effectiveness of the board.

Sum was previously an independent non-executive director of ComfortDelGro, where she served for 16 years - from Jan 1, 2007, to April 28, 2023. She retired from the role at the group’s annual general meeting (AGM) in April 2023.

Her previous careers include being the CEO of the Singapore Labour Foundation from January 2019 to June 2025 and CEO of NTUC Enterprise Co-operative Limited from October 2023 to March 2026.

title: Oil rises as Iran says it won’t soften Strait of Hormuz demands
article:
(Sept 28): Oil rose as Iran stuck to a seven-day proposal for reopening the crucial Strait of Hormuz rejected by US President Donald Trump, threatening further delays in the reopening of the crucial waterway.

Brent advanced above US$106 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate headed toward US$94. Tehran’s conditions are something Washington might have agreed to about a year ago, Trump told Axios in an interview on Sunday, saying that Iran has overplayed its hand. The US president said he expects negotiations to resume this week, Axios said.

Oil prices swung last week on mixed signals over diplomacy, recovering Middle East flows and uncertainty over US measures to curb record diesel prices, which Trump said Washington is looking at “very seriously.” Brent is up more than 70% this year, and on track for its third monthly gain, as the US-Iran conflict enters its eight month, adding to inflationary pressures.

Traders will continue to monitor physical flows through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world’s crude and liquefied natural gas before the start of the conflict. Trump said a “record amount” of oil was taken out of the strait on Saturday night, while the Fars news agency reported Iranian forces targeted ships using unauthorized routes through the waterway.

Regional tensions also remain elevated. Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said on Saturday that air defenses intercepted Houthi drones headed toward Riyadh and a missile targeting Khamis Mushait in the south. Alerts were also issued at Abha and Jazan, which host Aramco’s energy facilities.
